title: Helm Velocity and Incident Playbook - All Hands
summary: Quarterly all-hands focused on operational velocity, a refreshed incident playbook, hiring ramp, and a short metric pulse. Diego walked through a recently run post-incident checklist; we talked tradeoffs between faster rollouts and stricter canaries. Elena closed with priorities and an ask to managers to own team level runbooks.
topics: hiring update and hiring freeze discussion
next_steps: Managers to publish team runbooks to /docs/runbooks by 2026-05-22
SRE to publish new incident playbook and run the tabletop exercise week of 2026-05-18
People to share updated hiring plan and prioritization matrix by 2026-05-15

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-08 10:00 UTC | Duration: ~72 minutes | Host: Samir Patel
Attendees: Elena Park, Maya Chen, Diego Rivera, Priya Nair, Jonas Li, Ruth Gomez, Aaron Kim, and cross-company listeners (all-hands)

[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, um, thanks for joining. Quick housekeeping, recording is on. Today's agenda — velocity, incident playbook refresh, hiring, and a short metric pulse. Elena's going to kick off then Diego will walk through the post-incident lessons.

[00:42] Elena Park: Hi folks, really quick — first, thanks to SRE for the late night last month. I know that burned a lot of cycles. The point here is we want to increase rollout speed, but not at the cost of repeated incidents. So the playbook needs to make safer faster the default, not the other way around.

[01:10] Maya Chen: Totally. We looked at the canary telemetry and saw noisy flapping at the 90th p95 window which fooled our rollback automation. We need clearer thresholds and a little more human in the loop for cross-model deploys.

[01:45] Diego Rivera: I'll go through the postmortem highlights. Quick caveat — the transcription or auto notes, sometimes the product names get munged. The incident was triggered by a KV cache cold-spot combined with an inter-region routing change; essentially a cascade where the compactor process hit a perf cliff and then autoscaler spun up new nodes but they pulled the older quantized weights and that increased token latency.

[02:20] Priya Nair: Wait, Diego, can you repeat that — compactor? Did you mean cache compaction?

[02:29] Diego Rivera: Right, cache compaction; the transcriber sometimes says compactor. So cache compaction plus an older weight variant. The root cause chain: 1) config drift on the routing policy, 2) a stale model variant in the canary tier, 3) insufficient KV cache warming, 4) autoscaler and routing amplifying the latency.

[03:05] Jonas Li: On the config drift, what tooling do we have to detect divergence faster? Right now it's manual diff in infra repo which is too slow.

[03:20] Diego Rivera: Good question. We're piloting a config-sentry job that hashes deployed configs every 10 minutes and alerts on drift; it's in a sandbox cluster, we'll promote it after the tabletop.

[03:50] Samir Patel: A couple of themes from the runs — first, more prescriptive runbooks per team; second, canaries need stricter gating thresholds; third, a small cross-functional pact to avoid emergency ad-hoc routing changes during high traffic windows.

[04:24] Elena Park: Also, on the org level, I don't want us shipping less. I want safer shipping. That means better automation and clearer boundaries: who approves what, and what rollbacks look like.

[05:02] Audience question (unlabeled): Is there a plan to change the on-call rotation length? The last on-call week felt rough.

[05:15] Diego Rivera: We're shortening the heavy-duty on-call block from 7 to 5 days for platform engineers and adding a secondary pager for database/net bursts; also adding an incident responder shadow for new hires. We want to reduce cognitive load.

[06:02] Maya Chen: On rollouts, proposing we add a gray release step for heavy models — a slow traffic ramp with explicit KV warming stage. It costs a bit but reduces rollback frequency.

[06:37] Aaron Kim: Cost note — a gray release and KV warmers will incur additional infra spend. We modeled the Q2 delta and it's about a mid single digit percent increase if we do this for all heavyweight deploys. But the reduction in urgent incident hours looks worth it.

[07:12] Ruth Gomez: From People perspective, we also need to balance time off for on-call. Hiring pipeline timing is important — we have offers out and need to close quickly to reduce on-call pressure.

[07:45] Elena Park: Quick hiring update — we're accelerating for critical infra roles but pausing new IC headcount elsewhere. This is tactical for the quarter; we want to ensure coverage where the SLO delta matters most.

[08:10] Unlabeled: Will this be a hiring freeze or a re-prior?

[08:18] Elena Park: Re-prioritization, not a freeze. We will share a prioritized list. Ruth will circulate.

[08:40] Diego Rivera: Back to playbook specifics — we added a new detection checklist: circuit breaker metrics, KV miss rate, quantized weight mismatch, canary skew. Each item's threshold has an associated action: warn, page SRE, or auto-rollback. We debated auto-rollback; consensus was to keep it for hard failures but not for nuance (e.g., slight p95 drift).

[09:30] Priya Nair: How do we test the playbook? Tabletop exercises?

[09:37] Diego Rivera: Yes, tabletop for executives and a full run for platform engineers. Week of 2026-05-18 is target. We'll do at least two simulated incidents: one cache cold miss cascade and one region failover.

[10:05] Samir Patel: We're also going to publish a short 'what to do in first 10 mins' sheet for managers, engineers, and C-suite. Simple, bullet points.

[10:30] Audience (someone laughs): That 'first 10 minutes' doc will probably be the most read single doc ever.

[11:00] Maya Chen: Switching to metrics - Q2 pulse. High-level: request volume up 18% month-on-month, token consumption up 22%. Tail latency p95 saw a small uptick tied to a couple of heavy model queries. Error budget burn is within threshold but some routes are at 60% of monthly allowance.

[11:45] Aaron Kim: Finance perspective — revenue looks on plan; margin pressure is there but within forecast. If we keep these deploy protections we will see a small cost increase but expect long-term savings from fewer urgent interventions.

[12:20] Elena Park: Question for managers — are there any blockers to documentation or access to the runbooks?

[12:35] Jonas Li: For ML infra the blocker is time. We need templates and a small doc drive day to knock out initial drafts.

[12:55] Ruth Gomez: We'll schedule 'runbook sprints' — one-hour blocks where managers and writers pair to produce the first pass.

[13:20] Priya Nair: Quick product ask — product will own the rollout schedule for feature flag toggles that affect model behavior. We need to be included in the canary gating policy.

[13:40] Diego Rivera: Agreed. We'll have product signoff on gating thresholds for model-affecting flags.

[14:05] Unlabeled (murmur): Deck link?

[14:12] Samir Patel: Deck and the incident draft are in the shared drive — link posted in #all-hands and will be sent after the meeting. Please don't edit the canonical playbook until we finalize.

[14:40] Elena Park: People question — burnout signs are real. Managers, please ensure folks are rotating on-call and people are taking days off after on-call weeks. We'll also hire a contractor pool for surge support.

[15:05] Audience: Any change to SLAs or public comms?

[15:12] Aaron Kim: No change to public SLAs yet. We may change internal SLO definitions to be more granular so teams own smaller budgets.

[15:40] Maya Chen: A practical demo — quick screen share of the proposed gating console. (Transcription note: screen share audio low, some phrases unclear.) The gating console shows canary size, traffic percent, pass/fail thresholds, and an explicit KV warm stage.

[16:30] Samir Patel: We had a suggestion to add a deployment 'pause' API that external tools can call when they see anomalies. That will help automated controllers coordinate.

[16:50] Diego Rivera: We'll prototype pause API; it would be an idempotent call to stop new deploys in a cluster.

[17:12] Elena Park: On the org side — As we scale, our incident taxonomy should be standard across teams. Please use the short-form tags (latency, correctness, data, infra) in postmortems to make triage analytics easier.

[17:45] Audience: Will there be training for managers on the new playbook?

[17:52] Ruth Gomez: Yes, there will be a short manager training session and an on-call mini-course for new hires.

[18:20] Samir Patel: Quick Q&A lightning round — submit sticky notes in the doc.

[18:40] Unlabeled: Are we changing our private deployment offering or VPC controls because of this?

[18:50] Maya Chen: For Private/VPC customers we will not change guarantees, but we'll recommend tighter rollout policies and offer a runbook review as a professional services add-on.

[19:08] Diego Rivera: Also note: audit logs and KMS integration steps are part of the playbook for private customers. We have to ensure runbooks include escalation paths that respect customer security controls.

[19:40] Samir Patel: Final ask — managers publish runbooks, SRE publish playbook, People publish hiring list, and we'll run tabletop. We'll reconvene in a week for an ops sync.

[20:05] Elena Park: Thank you. Quick shoutout to the folks who jumped in during the outage — please make sure to add your learnings to the postmortem doc.

[20:20] Audience applause (murmur).

[20:35] Samir Patel: Closing notes — link to deck and incident draft posted; action items captured and owners assigned. If anyone has a question after, ping me or Diego. Thanks everyone.

End of recording.
